# Grammar

https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/reference/grammar

This page is a map of what the parser accepts: each keyword, each
statement, and where it may be written. The other chapters say what each
form means; this page says where it goes.

How to read the shapes on this page:

- A `text` block shows the shape of a form, not a program to copy.
- `…` stands for more of the same, and `|` separates alternatives.
- A word in lower case that is not a keyword, such as `expr`, `Type` or
  `name`, stands for something you write there.
- *Render block* means a block that holds elements and the statements that
  declare state: a page, a component, the `app`, a test, and every
  element's children. *Imperative block* means a block of statements that
  run: an action, a handler, an effect, a timer or a hook.

## Names

The case of a name says what it is:

| Kind of name | Case | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Declarations and statements | lower case | `page`, `state`, `for` |
| Elements, and the names declarations introduce | capitalised | `Button`, `UserCard`, `Todo` |
| Everything else | camelCase | `draft`, `isOpen`, `saveAll` |

A keyword has its meaning only where a statement starts. Everywhere else
it is an ordinary word, so every keyword works as a map key
(`{ action: "approve", type: "a" }`), a field name and an enum case.

A name the language already gives a meaning cannot be a program's own: the
words a statement is written with (`state`, `action`, `let`, `if`, `show`,
`match`, `style`, `on`, and the rest), the built-in functions, and the
values `env`, `params`, `locale`, `dir`, `now`, `viewport`, `query`,
`hash`, `theme`, `network` and `update`. Declared as a `state`, a prop, a
parameter, a loop item, a lambda's parameter or a `const`, one is an
`E118`. The names a handler brings (`event`, `e`, `value`, `key`) and the
browser's globals are yours to use. A program's own names may be written in
any script, Arabic included.

## Keywords

Each keyword, and where it starts a statement:

| Keyword | Where | Starts |
|---|---|---|
| `page`, `component`, `store`, `app`, `theme`, `type`, `enum`, `api`, `const`, `data`, `image`, `animation`, `test` | top of a file | a declaration |
| `state` | render block, store | a value that can change |
| `persist` | page, component, store | a value kept across visits |
| `derived` | render block, store | a value worked out from others |
| `effect`, with `cleanup` | render block, store | code that runs when what it reads changes, and its clean-up |
| `action` | render block, store | a named imperative block |
| `use` | render block | access to a store |
| `resource` | render block, store | a request whose state the page shows |
| `validate` | render block | the rules a state must pass |
| `socket`, `stream`, `channel`, `peer`, `worker` | render block, store | a connection the scope holds open |
| `every`, `after` | render block | a repeating or a one-off timer |
| `on key("…")`, `on resize`, and the other page events | top of a page, a component or `app` | a listener on the document or the window |
| `head` | page | tags for the document's head |
| `if`, `else`, `if let` | render or imperative block | a branch |
| `for`, with `in` and `by` | render or imperative block | a loop |
| `show` | render block | a block hidden, not removed, when its condition fails |
| `match` | render block, or a value | one arm, by a resource's state or an enum's case |
| `sequence`, `step` | render block | a timed group of enter animations |
| `slot`, `event`, `part` | component, before its elements | a slot, an event it fires, a part |
| `children` | component | where the caller's block goes |
| `style`, `transition`, `on` | element block | styles, transitions, handlers |
| `let`, `return` | imperative block | a local, and leaving with a value |
| `try`, `catch` | imperative block | error handling |
| `await` | imperative block, or a value | waiting for a promise |
| `emit` | imperative block of a component | firing one of its events |
| `expect`, `click`, `type`, `press` | test | a step a test checks or performs |

## Declarations

These forms are written at the top of a file, and nowhere else:

```text
page Name(path: "/", title: …, description: …, image: …, image_alt: …, type: …,
          noindex: …, lang: "…", translates: Page, layout: Component(…),
          guard: expr, redirect: "/…", paths: expr, param: Type, …) { render block }
component Name(_ positional: Type, prop: Type = default, …) { component body }
store Name(scope: .app | .session | .route, eager: Bool) { store body }
app { render block }
theme Name { token: value … }
type Name { field: Type = default, … }        type Name = Other { … }
enum Name { case, case(part: Type, …), … }
api Name(base: expr, …) { settings  on request|response|error(x) { … }  endpoints }
api Name from "spec.json" (base: expr)
const NAME: Type = expr
data name: Type = "file.json"
image name = "picture.jpg"
animation Name { from { css } 50% { css } to { css } }
test "name"(data: { … }) { render block and test steps }
```

A `///` comment before a declaration, a prop, a field, an event, an
endpoint, or a `state`, `persist`, `derived` or `action` of a page, a
component or a store is its documentation.

A store's body holds `state`, `persist`, `derived`, `effect`, `action`,
`resource` and the connections (`socket`, `stream`, `channel`, `peer`,
`worker`).

## Render blocks

A page, a component, the app, a test and every element's children hold
these statements:

| Statement | Form |
|---|---|
| state | `state name: Type = expr` |
| persisted state | `persist name: Type = expr { in: .local \| .session \| .name  key: expr  version: n  sync: Bool  migrate n -> n+1 { expr } }` — a page, a component or a store |
| derived | `derived name = expr` |
| effect | `effect { imperative  cleanup { imperative } }` |
| action | `action name(param: Type, …) { imperative }` |
| store | `use Store` |
| resource | `resource name: Type = fetch(url, options)` or `= Api.endpoint(args)` |
| validation | `validate name { rule(args) "message"  custom "message" { expr }  async "message" { expr } }` |
| connection | `socket name = ws(url, …) { send T  receive T  on message(m) { … }  on open { … } }`, `stream name = sse(…)`, `channel name = broadcast(…)`, `peer name = rtc(signal: …, …)`, `worker name = spawn(path, …) { on message(m) { … } }` |
| timer | `every(interval) { imperative }`, `after(interval) { imperative }` |
| key | `on key("ctrl+k", e) { imperative }` |
| page event | `on keydown(e) { … }`, `on resize { … }` — and `keyup`, `scroll`, `hashchange`, `popstate`, `online`, `offline`, `message`, `storage`, `visibilitychange`, `blur`, `focus` — at the top of a page, a component or `app` |
| head | `head { meta(…)  link(…)  script(…) }` — a page only |
| conditional | `if cond { … } else if cond { … } else { … }`, `if let x = expr { … }` |
| loop | `for item, index in list by key { … }` |
| visibility | `show cond { … }` |
| choice | `match expr { .case(a) { … }  loading { … }  error(e) { … }  ready(v) { … }  else { … } }` |
| orchestration | `sequence { step(after: "120ms") { … } }` |
| set-up | `Store.action(args)` — a call, run once when the block renders |
| element | `Name(positional, prop: value).flag.flag { block }` |
| slot use | `children`, `slotName`, `slotName(value: expr)` — a component only |

A connection's options may also be written inside its block, one
`name: value` to a line.

## Component bodies

A component's body is a render block, and before its elements it may
declare:

```text
slot                                  the default slot, placed with `children`
slot name                             a named slot
slot name(value: Type, …)             a scoped slot
event name(param: Type, …)            an event it fires with `emit`
part Name(props) { render block }     a part, called as `Component.Name`
```

## Element blocks

An element's block holds these, in this order, each optional:

```text
Name(…).flags {
    style { declarations }
    transition { property: duration easing … }
    on event(e) { imperative }
    slotName(params) { render block }      a slot fill, on a component call
    children
}
```

## Imperative blocks

Actions, handlers, effects, timers and hooks hold these statements:

| Statement | Form |
|---|---|
| assignment | `name = expr`, `a.b = expr`, `list[i] = expr` |
| local | `let name: Type = expr`, `let { a, b } = expr`, `let [x, y] = expr` |
| call | `f(args)`, `Store.action(args)`, `list.push(x)`, `navigate("/…")`, `log(…)` |
| emit | `emit event(args)` — a component only |
| return | `return`, `return expr` |
| conditional | `if … else …`, `if let …` |
| loop | `for x in list { … }`, `for x, i in list { … }`, `for n in 1..=10 { … }` |
| error handling | `try { … } catch e { … }` |
| waiting | `await expr` — makes the action asynchronous |

`let`, `return` and `emit` written in a render block are an error that
says to move them into a handler, an action or an effect.

## Style blocks and themes

A `style` block holds CSS declarations, one to a line:

```text
style {
    property: raw css value               to the end of the line, a `;`, or two spaces and the next declaration
    property: {expr}px $token             a live value, a design token
    --custom-property: value
    &:hover { declarations }              nested rules, as CSS nesting writes them
    @media (…) { declarations }           and `@md { }` for a breakpoint, `@container (…) { }`
}
```

A theme's body is the same declarations, without nesting.

## Test steps

A `test` holds render statements and these steps, run in the order
written:

| Step | Form |
|---|---|
| check | `expect "text"`, `expect not "text"` |
| click | `click "name"` |
| type | `type "text" into "name"` |
| key | `press "Key"`, `press "Key" in "name"` |

## Expressions

The operators, from weakest to strongest binding:

| Level | Operators |
|---|---|
| 1 | `..` `..=` (ranges) |
| 2 | `??` |
| 3 | `\|\|` |
| 4 | `&&` |
| 5 | `==` `!=` (`!==` too) |
| 6 | `<` `<=` `>` `>=` |
| 7 | `+` `-` |
| 8 | `*` `/` `%` |
| 9 | unary `!` `-`, `await` |
| 10 | calls `f(…)`, fields `a.b`, `a?.b`, methods `a.m(…)`, `a?.m(…)`, indexes `a[i]`, `a?.[i]`, flags |

So `1..n + 1` is `1..(n + 1)`, and `a ?? b || c` is `a ?? (b || c)`.
Operators of one level group from the left: `a - b - c` is `(a - b) - c`.

These forms are expressions too:

- `if c { a } else { b }`, which is `null` when there is no `else` and `c`
  fails;
- `if let x = v { a } else { b }`;
- `match v { .case { a } else { b } }`;
- lambdas `x => expr`, `(a, b) => expr` and `() => expr`;
- spreads `...x` in a list, a map or a call's arguments.

A call's named arguments (`due.plus(days: 3)`) are gathered into one map,
passed last. [Expressions](/reference/expressions) explains each form.

## Literals

| Kind | Written |
|---|---|
| String | `"text {splice} {value:.style(option)}"`, raw `#"…"#`, block `"""…"""` |
| Number | `42`, `3.14` |
| Bool, null | `true`, `false`, `null` |
| List, map | `[a, b]`, `{ key: value, "Quoted-Key": value, ...other }` |
| Regex | `/pattern/flags` |
| Date, time | `@2026-03-14`, `@09:30`, `@2026-03-14T09:30Z` |
| Duration | `250.ms`, `5.seconds`, `90.minutes`, `2.hours`, `3.days`, `1.weeks` |
| Money | `€12.99`, `$9.99`, `£4.50` |
| Colour | `#0F766E` |
| Enum case | `.name`, `.name(payload)` |
| Design token | `$name` |

## Comments

`// to the end of the line`, `/* across lines */`, and `///` documentation.

## Layout

A `.wf` file writes blocks in braces. A `.wfx` file writes them by
indentation: a line indented deeper than the one before opens a block, and
a dedent closes it. Braces written by hand still work inside a line
([Language basics](/learn/04-language-basics#two-layouts-wf-and-wfx)).
Statements need no separator, on one line either: the parser finds where
one ends. Two on one line read best apart by a `;` or two spaces
(`count = 0; log(count)`).

## Next

[Browser support](/reference/browser-support): which browsers a WebFluent site targets, and what each newer platform feature falls back to where a browser lacks it.



---

# Project structure

https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/reference/project

A WebFluent project is a config file and a folder of sources that the
compiler reads as one program. The folders are a convention for you and
your team; the compiler does not care where a declaration lives. This
chapter explains how a project is laid out and read, then shows you how to
add files, choose what to commit and keep a growing project in order.

In this chapter:

- the conventional layout, and which files are required;
- how the compiler merges every file into one program, and what that means
  for names;
- what happens to the files that are not `.wf`;
- how to generate starter files, what to commit, and how to organise a
  project as it grows.

## The layout

This is the layout `wf init` starts from, with every kind of file a project
can hold:

```text
my-site/
├── AGENTS.md               the language reference, for a coding agent (`wf init` writes it)
├── webfluent.app.json      the config (see Configuration)
├── .env                    build-time values, not committed (see Environments)
├── src/
│   ├── App.wf              the app shell and the Router
│   ├── theme.wf            themes
│   ├── types.wf            shared types, enums, constants, data
│   ├── api.wf              services
│   ├── pages/              one page per file
│   ├── components/         components
│   ├── stores/             stores
│   ├── styles.css          your own stylesheets, anywhere under src/
│   ├── tilt.js             your own scripts, anywhere under src/
│   ├── translations/       en.json, ar.json (with "i18n" in the config)
│   ├── posts.json          data files a `data` declaration reads
│   └── about.md            Markdown pages
├── public/                 copied to the build's root: favicon, fonts, images
├── tests/                  `test` declarations, and __snapshots__/
└── build/                  what `wf build` writes (not committed)
```

Only two things are required: `webfluent.app.json` and one `.wf` or `.wfx`
file under `src/`. Everything else is convention. The config is covered in
[Configuration](/reference/config), and `.env` in
[Environments and secrets](/recipes/environments-and-secrets).

## One program, with no imports

The compiler reads every `.wf` and `.wfx` file under `src/` and merges them
into a single program. A page uses a component declared in another file, and
a component uses a store, by name. There is nothing to import.

For example, a component declared in `src/components/PriceCard.wf` and a
page in `src/pages/Pricing.wf` work together with no import between them.
Here they are in one block:

```wf
// In src/components/PriceCard.wf
component PriceCard(_ plan: String, price: Number) {
    Card {
        Text(plan).bold
        Text(format(price, .currency))
    }
}

// In src/pages/Pricing.wf
page Pricing(path: "/pricing", title: "Pricing", description: "Plans and prices.") {
    Heading("Pricing").h1
    PriceCard("Team", price: 49)
}
```

The compiler reads `App.wf` (or `App.wfx`) first, then the rest in path
order. The order matters for nothing but the order of equal things in the
output.

`use Store` at the top of a page or component says that it reads that
store. It documents the dependency for the reader and the editor; it does
not scope anything, and a page reads a store by name with or without it.

## Names across a project

Because every file is one program, the namespace is global. Two
components, two pages, two stores, two types or two constants with one name
is an `E102` error, naming both places.

The conventions that keep names apart:

- **Declared names are PascalCase**: pages, components, stores, types,
  enums, themes, services and animations.
- **Constants are UPPER_SNAKE** by convention: `API`, `PAGE_SIZE`.
- **A page's name is its identity, not its title.** Add a suffix when the
  name would collide with a component: `page PostPage` beside
  `component Post`.
- **A component that one page uses** can live in that page's file.

## Files that are not `.wf`

The build reads other files too. What each becomes:

| File | Where | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `*.css` | anywhere under `src/` | bundled into `styles.css`, in path order, after the built-ins' rules |
| `*.js` | anywhere under `src/` | copied to `js/` as written and linked on every page before the compiled code; its top-level names are in scope ([Call your own JavaScript](/recipes/call-your-own-script)) |
| `*.md` | under `src/` | a page ([Content](/recipes/markdown-pages)) |
| `*.json` | named by a `data` declaration | a constant, read at build time |
| images | named by an `image` declaration | resized, hashed files and a `<picture>` ([Add a picture](/recipes/add-a-picture)) |
| `translations/*.json` | the `i18n.dir` | the locale tables ([Translate a site](/recipes/translate-a-site)) |
| anything | `public/` | copied as it is to the build's root: `public/favicon.svg` is `/favicon.svg` |

## Generate a starter file

To add a page, a component or a store with the boilerplate written for
you, run `wf generate`:

```bash
wf generate page Pricing
wf generate component PriceCard
wf generate store Cart
```

Each command writes a starter declaration in the conventional folder:

| Command | Writes |
|---|---|
| `wf generate page Pricing` | `src/pages/Pricing.wf`, with `path: "/pricing"`, a title, a description and an `h1` |
| `wf generate component PriceCard` | `src/components/PriceCard.wf` |
| `wf generate store Cart` | `src/stores/cart.wf` |

In a project written in `.wfx`, the files are `.wfx`. `wf generate` never
overwrites a file: when one exists, it says so and stops. Add `-d DIR` to
generate into a project other than the current directory.

## Choose what to commit

Commit the sources and the config:

- `webfluent.app.json`
- `src/`
- `public/`
- `tests/`, with its `__snapshots__/`

Leave out what the build writes and what is private. Add these lines to
`.gitignore`:

```text
build/
.wf-cache/
.wf-sizes.json
.env
```

`.wf-cache/` holds resized images between builds. `.wf-sizes.json` records
what the last build weighed, for `wf build --stats` to compare against.
`.env` holds build-time values that may be private.

## Organise a growing project

As a project grows, these habits keep it readable:

- **Group by feature once folders get long.** A `src/billing/` folder that
  holds the billing pages, components, store and types reads better than
  four folders that each hold a slice of it. The compiler does not mind
  either way.
- **Put each service in one place.** Write one `api` per backend, in its
  own file, with the types its endpoints return beside it.
- **Keep shared types together**, in a `types.wf` per area, so the
  editor's go-to-definition lands somewhere predictable.
- **Document as you declare.** A `///` comment above a component, a prop,
  an event or a type shows on hover and in `wf docs`, the gallery of
  everything the project declares.
- **Hold every file to the formatter.** `wf fmt --check` in CI keeps every
  file in one layout ([Testing](/learn/16-testing#run-the-checks-in-ci)).

## Quick reference

| Topic | Rule |
|---|---|
| Required files | `webfluent.app.json` and one `.wf` or `.wfx` file under `src/` |
| Reading order | `App.wf` first, then the rest in path order |
| Imports | none: every declaration is in scope by name |
| `use Store` | documents a dependency; scopes nothing |
| Duplicate names | `E102`, naming both places |
| `public/` | copied to the build's root as it is |
| Starter files | `wf generate page`, `component` or `store`, then the name |
| Not committed | `build/`, `.wf-cache/`, `.wf-sizes.json`, `.env` |

## Next

- [Static or single-page](/about/static-or-single-page): choose how the project
  builds.
- [CLI](/reference/cli): every `wf` command.



---

# Built-ins

https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/reference/built-ins

This page lists everything a program can call or read without declaring
it: the functions the language adds, the browser values it keeps current,
the methods of strings, lists and numbers, the built-in types, and the
browser's own globals. [Expressions](/reference/expressions) explains how to use
them; this page is for looking one up.

Each function and value has an entry in the same order: what it is, its
signature, its parameters and what it returns, where it may be written,
and an example. An example of one line is a fragment of a page; the names
it reads are assumed to be declared.

## Functions

The functions, in alphabetical order:

| Function | Does |
|---|---|
| [`after(interval) { }`](#after) | Runs a block once, after a delay |
| [`ago(date)`](#ago) | The distance from now, in words |
| [`animate(element, name, duration)`](#animate) | Plays an animation on an element handle |
| [`beacon(url, data)`](#beacon) | Sends a small post that survives the page unloading |
| [`broadcast(name)`](#broadcast) | Opens a channel the site's other tabs hear |
| [`every(interval) { }`](#every) | Runs a block repeatedly |
| [`fetch(url, options)`](#fetch) | Sends a request through the same engine as `api` |
| [`format(value, .style, option)`](#format) | A number, date or money as text, in the locale |
| [`keyIs(event, combination)`](#keyis) | Whether a key event is a shortcut |
| [`keyLabel(combination)`](#keylabel) | A shortcut as this system writes it |
| [`log(x)`](#log) | Prints a value to the console |
| [`navigate(path)`](#navigate) | Moves to a route |
| [`optimistic(holder, change)`](#optimistic) | Shows a change now, and takes it back if the action throws |
| [`replayAnimation(element, name)`](#replayanimation) | Plays an element's animation again |
| [`rtc(signal: …)`](#rtc) | Opens a data channel to another reader's page |
| [`sanitize(html)`](#sanitize) | Markup through an allow-list |
| [`setLocale(locale)`](#setlocale) | Switches the locale, and the direction with it |
| [`setTheme(choice)`](#settheme) | Switches between light, dark and the system's choice |
| [`spawn(path)`](#spawn) | Starts a script of `public/` in a worker |
| [`sse(url)`](#sse) | Opens a stream of server-sent events |
| [`t("key", values)`](#t) | A translation |
| [`uuid()`](#uuid) | A fresh `Uuid` |
| [`ws(url)`](#ws) | Opens a WebSocket |

Every name in this list but `spawn` belongs to the language: a `state`,
prop, parameter, loop item or `const` with one of these names is an
`E118`. `spawn` means something only after `worker name =`.

### `after`

Runs a block once, after a delay, unless its scope leaves first.

Signature: `after(interval) { statements }`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `interval` | `Number` (milliseconds) or `Duration` | How long to wait |

Returns nothing. Where: a render block — a page, a component, a branch, a
list item. The timer is cancelled when the block that holds it leaves.
See [Timers](/learn/07-state-and-reactivity#timers).

```wf
after(3.seconds) { banner = null }
```

### `ago`

The distance between a date and now, in words, in the reader's locale.

Signature: `ago(date)`, `ago(date, moment)` → `String`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | `Date`, `DateTime` or an ISO 8601 string | The moment to describe |
| `moment` | the same, optional | What to measure from, in place of now |

Returns `now` under 45 seconds, then `5 minutes ago`, `yesterday`,
`in 2 weeks`, and so on. An unreadable date gives `""`. Where: anywhere. It
is the same as `format(date, .relative)`.

```wf
Text("Posted {ago(post.published)}").muted
```

### `animate`

Plays a named animation on an element you hold a handle on.

Signature: `animate(element, name, duration)` → a handle

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | a `ref:` handle | The element to animate |
| `name` | `String` | A built-in animation (`"pulse"`, `"shake"`, …) or one an `animation` declares |
| `duration` | `String` such as `"400ms"` | How long it plays |

Returns a handle with `play()`, `cancel()` and `finished` (a promise). It
plays as soon as it is made. Where: handlers and actions. See
[Motion](/recipes/drive-an-animation).

```wf
Card(ref: panel) { on mouseenter { animate(panel, "pulse", "400ms") } }
```

### `beacon`

Sends a small `POST` that the browser delivers even while the page is
unloading.

Signature: `beacon(url, data)` → `Bool`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `String` | Where to send it |
| `data` | `Map` or `String` | The body; a map is sent as JSON |

Returns whether the browser accepted the send. Where: anywhere, usually a
handler. See [Send a message as the page unloads](/recipes/send-on-unload).

```wf
beacon("/analytics", { event: "checkout", value: total })
```

### `broadcast`

Opens a channel that every tab and window of the site on this browser
hears.

Signature: `channel name = broadcast(channelName) { on message(m) { … } }`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `channelName` | `String` | The channel; tabs that open the same name hear each other |

Returns a channel handle with `.post(value)`, `.messages`, `.last(kind)`,
`.state` and `.close()`. Where: only after `channel name =`, in a page, a
component or a store. The channel closes when its scope leaves. See
[Talk to the site's other tabs](/recipes/talk-between-tabs).

```wf
channel cart = broadcast("cart") { on message(m) { Cart.merge(m) } }
```

### `every`

Runs a block repeatedly until its scope leaves.

Signature: `every(interval) { statements }`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `interval` | `Number` (milliseconds) or `Duration` | The time between runs |

Returns nothing. Where: a render block. The timer stops when its page,
branch or list item leaves. See
[Timers](/learn/07-state-and-reactivity#timers).

```wf
every(1.seconds) { elapsed = elapsed + 1 }
```

### `fetch`

Sends a request through the same engine an `api` uses: retries, caching
and cancelling come with it.

Signature: `fetch(url, options)` → the parsed response body

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `String` | The address; a value spliced into it is encoded |
| `options` | `Map`, optional | `method`, `headers`, `body`; a map given as `body` is sent as JSON |

Returns the parsed JSON body, and throws when the response fails. Where:
`await fetch(…)` in an action or a handler, or `resource name = fetch(…)`,
which adds `on:` and the other options of a resource. `window.fetch` is the
browser's own, untouched. See
[Fetch on demand with `await fetch`](/learn/15-data#fetch-on-demand-with-await-fetch).

```wf
let rows = await fetch("/api/rows?page={page}", { method: "GET" })
```

### `format`

Writes a number, a date or money as text, in the reader's locale.

Signature: `format(value)`, `format(value, .style)`, `format(value, .style, option)`, `format(value, "pattern")` → `String`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `Number`, `Money`, `Date`, `DateTime` or an ISO string | What to write |
| `style` | `.number` (default), `.integer`, `.decimal`, `.currency`, `.percent`, `.compact`, `.date`, `.time`, `.datetime`, `.relative` | How to write it |
| `option` | depends on the style | Places for `.decimal` (2) and `.percent` (0); a currency code for `.currency` (`"USD"`); `"short"`, `"medium"`, `"long"` or `"full"` for the date styles |
| `pattern` | `String` | A date pattern of `yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h mm ss a` |

Returns the text. The locale is the i18n locale when the project has one,
and the document's language otherwise; a change of locale redraws it. A
`Money` value needs no style. In a string, `{value:.style(option)}` is the
same call. Where: anywhere. See
[`format` and `ago`](/reference/expressions#format-and-ago).

```wf
Text(format(price, .currency, "EUR"))
```

### `keyIs`

Whether a key event is a given combination — for a table of shortcuts held
as data.

Signature: `keyIs(event, combination)` → `Bool`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `event` | a key event | The event a `keydown` handler receives |
| `combination` | `String` | Modifiers and a key, as `on key("…")` writes them: `"mod+s"`, `"shift+ArrowDown"` |

Returns `true` when the event is that combination. `mod` is ⌘ on a Mac and
Ctrl elsewhere. Where: handlers. See [Keys](/learn/08-events#keys).

```wf
Input(bind: draft, label: "Note") { on keydown(e) { if keyIs(e, "mod+s") { save() } } }
```

### `keyLabel`

A combination as this system writes it, for a menu or a tooltip.

Signature: `keyLabel(combination)` → `String`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `combination` | `String` | As `keyIs` takes it |

Returns `⇧⌘P` on a Mac and `Ctrl+Shift+P` elsewhere for
`"mod+shift+p"`. Where: anywhere. A `Menu.Item`'s or a `Tooltip`'s
`shortcut:` is written this way for you.

```wf
Text("Search: {keyLabel("mod+k")}").muted
```

### `log`

Prints a value to the browser's console.

Signature: `log(value)`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | any | The value to print. For several, splice them into one string, `log("{a} {b}")`, or call `console.log(a, b)` |

Returns nothing. Where: actions, handlers, effects and timers. A `Secret`
passed to it is a `T12`.

```wf
log("saved {items.length} items")
```

### `navigate`

Moves to a route, as a click on a `Link` would.

Signature: `navigate(path)`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `String` | A site-relative path; a value spliced into it is encoded |

Returns nothing. In a single-page build the router draws the new page; in
a static build it loads the page's own HTML file. A literal path no page
matches is an `R01`, and a scheme a browser would run is refused. Where:
actions and handlers. See
[Links and navigation](/learn/05-pages-and-routing#links-and-navigation).

```wf
Button("Open") { on click { navigate("/orders/{order.id}") } }
```

### `optimistic`

Shows a change at once, before the server agrees. If anything later in the
action throws, the change is taken back.

Signature: `optimistic(holder, change)`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `holder` | a state, or a store's state | What to change |
| `change` | a lambda from the old value to the new one | The change to show |

Returns a handle with `rollback()`. Where: actions. See
[Show a change before the server agrees](/learn/15-data#show-a-change-before-the-server-agrees).

```wf
optimistic(Todos.items, items => items.filter(i => i.id != id))
```

### `replayAnimation`

Plays again an animation the element already has, such as its enter
animation.

Signature: `replayAnimation(element, name)`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `element` | an element, such as `e.currentTarget` | The element to animate |
| `name` | `String` | The animation, such as `"fadeIn"` |

Returns nothing. Where: handlers. See
[Motion](/recipes/drive-an-animation).

```wf
Card.outlined.fadeIn { on mouseenter(e) { replayAnimation(e.currentTarget, "fadeIn") } }
```

### `rtc`

Opens a WebRTC data channel straight to another reader's page.

Signature: `peer name = rtc(signal: send, initiator: Bool, ice: [servers]) { on message(m) { … } }`

| Option | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `signal` | a lambda, required | How what this side must tell the other reaches it |
| `initiator` | `Bool` | Whether this side makes the offer; one side must |
| `ice` | `[Map]` | The servers that help readers on different networks connect; none by default |

Returns a peer handle with `.send(value)`, `.signal(message)` (hand it what
the other side sent), `.state`, `.messages` and `.close()`. Where: only after
`peer name =`. See
[Connect two readers' pages](/recipes/connect-two-readers).

```wf
peer link = rtc(signal: m => lobby.post(m), initiator: query.host == "1") { on message(m) { heard = m.text } }
```

### `sanitize`

Passes markup through an allow-list of elements and attributes, for
`Unsafe.Html`.

Signature: `sanitize(html)` → `String`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `html` | `String` | Markup from outside the project |

Returns the markup without scripts, styles, frames, forms, `on*`
attributes, or an `href` or `src` a browser would run. It runs at build
time and in the browser from the same list. Where: anywhere. See
[Show markup you did not write](/about/security#one-door-for-markup).

```wf
Unsafe.Html(sanitize(post.body))
```

### `setLocale`

Switches the page to another locale, and its direction with it.

Signature: `setLocale(locale)`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `locale` | `String` | A locale `i18n.locales` lists, such as `"ar"`; `-u-nu-arab` or `-u-nu-latn` names the digits |

Returns nothing. Every `t(…)`, `format` and `ago` redraws, and an RTL
locale sets `dir="rtl"`. A literal locale the config does not list is an
`I04`. Where: actions, handlers and effects. See
[i18n](/recipes/translate-a-site#switch-the-locale).

```wf
Button("العربية") { on click { setLocale("ar") } }
```

### `setTheme`

Switches between the light theme, the dark one, and whatever the system
asks for, and keeps the choice across visits.

Signature: `setTheme(choice)`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `choice` | `String` | `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"` |

Returns nothing. The browser value `theme` reads the choice. Any other
number of arguments is a `T10`. Where: actions and handlers. See
[Dark mode](/learn/13-styling#dark-mode).

```wf
Button("Dark") { on click { setTheme("dark") } }
```

### `spawn`

Starts a script of `public/` in a worker beside the page.

Signature: `worker name = spawn(path, restart: n, timeout: ms, type: .module) { on message(m) { … } }`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `String` | The script's site-relative address; a missing file is a `D01` |
| `restart` | `Number` | How many times a crash starts it again |
| `timeout` | `Number` | How long a request waits, in milliseconds (10 s unset) |
| `type` | `.module` | Starts a module worker |

Returns a worker handle with `.request(method, params, options)`,
`.send(value)`, `.last(kind)`, `.pending`, `.state` and `.restart()`.
Where: only after `worker name =`, in a page, a component or a store. See
[Run a script in a worker](/recipes/run-a-worker).

```wf
worker css = spawn("/workers/css.js", restart: 1) { on message(m) { problems = m.items } }
```

### `sse`

Opens a stream of server-sent events, which resumes where it was after a
drop.

Signature: `stream name = sse(url, events: [names])`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `String` | The stream's address |
| `events` | `[String]` | The named events to listen for |

Returns a stream handle with `.messages`, `.last(kind)`, `.state`,
`.error` and `.close()`. Where: only after `stream name =`. See
[Listen to server-sent events](/recipes/server-sent-events).

```wf
stream ticks = sse("/events", events: ["price", "status"])
```

### `t`

A translation of a key, in the reader's locale.

Signature: `t(key)`, `t(key, values)` → `String`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `String` | A key of the translation files |
| `values` | `Map`, optional | Values for the message's `{placeholders}`; `count` picks a plural form |

Returns the message. A literal key no locale has is an `I01`; a value the
message does not use, or a placeholder the call does not pass, is an
`I02`. Where: anywhere. See [`t("key")`](/recipes/translate-a-site#translate-text-with-t).

```wf
Text(t("cart.items", { count: Cart.count }))
```

### `uuid`

A fresh random identifier.

Signature: `uuid()` → `Uuid`

It takes no parameters. Where: anywhere, usually an action that makes a
record.

```wf
items = items.concat([Todo(id: uuid(), title: draft)])
```

### `ws`

Opens a WebSocket, which reconnects with backoff and keeps itself alive.

Signature: `socket name = ws(url, protocols: [names], heartbeat: duration) { send T  receive T  on message(m) { … } }`

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `String` | A `ws:` or `wss:` address |
| `protocols` | `[String]` | The subprotocols to offer |
| `heartbeat` | `Duration` | How often to ping a quiet line |

Returns a socket handle with `.send(value)`, `.messages`, `.last(kind)`,
`.state`, `.error`, `.closure` and `.close()`. Where: only after
`socket name =`. See [Open a socket](/recipes/open-a-socket).

```wf
socket chat = ws("wss://example.com/chat", heartbeat: 20.seconds) { on message(m) { Feed.add(m) } }
```

## Browser values

The language keeps these values current and lets every page, component and
store read them. Each is a name the language owns: declaring a `state`,
prop or parameter with one of these names is an `E118`.

| Value | Holds |
|---|---|
| [`viewport`](#viewport) | The window's size and breakpoints |
| [`query`](#query) | The address's query string |
| [`hash`](#hash) | The address's fragment |
| [`theme`](#theme) | The reader's light or dark choice |
| [`now`](#now) | The current moment |
| [`network`](#network) | The connection's state |
| [`update`](#update) | A new version of an offline site |
| [`locale`, `dir`](#locale-and-dir) | The reader's language and its direction |
| [`params`](#params) | The route's parameters |

### `viewport`

The window's size, and which breakpoints it is past.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `.width`, `.height` | `Number` | The size in CSS pixels |
| `.sm`, `.md`, `.lg`, `.xl` | `Bool` | Whether the width is at least that breakpoint's token |

It follows `matchMedia`, so a breakpoint field changes once when its answer
changes, not on every pixel of a resize.

```wf
if viewport.md { Sidebar { Sidebar.Item(to: "/", icon: "home") { Text("Home") } } }
```

### `query`

The address's query string, as a map from each key to its value.

A key the address lacks reads as `null`, so `query.tab ?? "all"` gives a
default.

```wf
Text("Showing {query.tab ?? "all"}")
```

### `hash`

The address's fragment, without the `#`. It is `""` when there is none.

```wf
if hash == "pricing" { Text("You followed a link to pricing.") }
```

### `theme`

The reader's choice: `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"`. `setTheme` changes
it.

```wf
Button("Light", outlined: theme != "light") { on click { setTheme("light") } }
```

### `now`

The current moment, as a `DateTime` that keeps itself current — every
minute by default.

Signature: `now`, `now(every: interval)` → `DateTime`

Read it where it is shown or in a `derived` value. A `state` takes it once,
so `state opened = now` keeps the moment the page opened (`X06`). See
[`now`](/learn/12-types#now).

```wf
Text("It is {now(every: 1.seconds).time()}")
```

### `network`

The state of the reader's connection.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `.online` | `Bool` | Whether the browser has a connection |
| `.effectiveType` | `String` | `"4g"`, `"3g"`, and so on |
| `.saveData` | `Bool` | Whether the reader asked to save data |
| `.downlink` | `Number` | The estimated bandwidth, in megabits a second |
| `.queued` | `Number` | Writes waiting for the connection, with `offline.sync` |

```wf
if !network.online { Alert("You are offline — changes are queued.").warning }
```

### `update`

A new version of a site that has `offline` in its config.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `.available` | `Bool` | Whether a new version has installed and is waiting |
| `.apply()` | — | Takes the new version and reloads the page once |

```wf
if update.available { Button("Reload for the new version") { on click { update.apply() } } }
```

### `locale` and `dir`

The reader's current locale (`"en"`, `"ar"`) and its direction (`"ltr"` or
`"rtl"`). Both follow `setLocale`.

```wf
Text("Reading in {locale}, {dir}")
```

### `params`

The current route's parameters, by name. A page also receives each one as
a typed parameter of its own, which is usually the better way to read it.

```wf
Text("Order {params.id}")
```

## String methods

A string has the browser's methods and five of WebFluent's own. A method
it has neither of is a `T16`, with the nearest one it has.

WebFluent's own:

| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `capitalize()` | The text with its first letter in upper case |
| `truncate(n)` | The first `n` characters, followed by `…` when the text was longer |
| `dedent()` | The text without the indentation its lines share, and without blank first and last lines |
| `lines()` | A list of its lines, however they end |
| `words()` | A list of its words, split on runs of whitespace |

The browser's: `length`, `trim()`, `trimStart()`, `trimEnd()`,
`toLowerCase()`, `toUpperCase()`, `toLocaleLowerCase()`,
`toLocaleUpperCase()`, `includes(s)`, `startsWith(s)`, `endsWith(s)`,
`indexOf(s)`, `lastIndexOf(s)`, `search(re)`, `slice(a, b)`,
`substring(a, b)`, `substr(a, n)`, `charAt(i)`, `charCodeAt(i)`,
`codePointAt(i)`, `at(i)`, `replace(a, b)`, `replaceAll(a, b)`,
`split(sep)`, `match(re)`, `matchAll(re)`, `concat(s)`, `padStart(n, c)`,
`padEnd(n, c)`, `repeat(n)`, `normalize()`, `localeCompare(other)`,
`isWellFormed()`, `toWellFormed()`, `toString()`, `valueOf()`.

`contains(s)` is accepted for `includes(s)`, and `toUpper()` and
`toLower()` for `toUpperCase()` and `toLowerCase()`.

```wf
derived preview = post.body.dedent().lines().first() ?? ""
```

## List methods

A list has the browser's array methods and seven of WebFluent's own.

WebFluent's own:

| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `sortBy(f)` | A sorted copy, ordered by what `f` returns for each item |
| `groupBy(f)` | A map from what `f` returns, as a string, to the items that returned it |
| `unique()` | A copy without repeats; records are compared by their contents |
| `take(n)` | The first `n` items |
| `first()`, `last()` | The first or last item, or `null` when the list is empty |
| `sum()` | The total of a list of numbers |
| `remove(i)` | The list without the item at index `i`; out of range, an unchanged copy |

The browser's: `length`, `map(f)`, `filter(f)`, `find(f)`, `findIndex(f)`,
`findLast(f)`, `findLastIndex(f)`, `some(f)`, `every(f)`, `includes(x)`,
`indexOf(x)`, `lastIndexOf(x)`, `join(sep)`, `slice(a, b)`,
`concat(other)`, `reverse()`, `sort(f)`, `reduce(f, init)`,
`reduceRight(f, init)`, `forEach(f)`, `flat()`, `flatMap(f)`, `fill(x)`,
`copyWithin(t, a, b)`, `entries()`, `keys()`, `values()`, `at(i)`,
`with(i, x)`, `toReversed()`, `toSorted(f)`, `toSpliced(…)`, `toString()`,
`toLocaleString()`; and, in an action or a handler, `push(x)`, `pop()`,
`shift()`, `unshift(x)` and `splice(i, n)`. `contains(x)` is accepted for
`includes(x)`.

How the methods treat a state:

- `sort` and `reverse` read in an expression work on a copy, so reading a
  sorted list never changes it.
- `push(x)`, `remove(i)` and `sort(f)` as a statement give the state a new
  list, so whatever reads it repaints and a `persist` writes it.

```wf
derived leaders = players.sortBy(p => -p.score).take(3)
```

Every one of WebFluent's own helpers also runs at build time, so the
pre-rendered page shows its result. A member something declares wins over
a helper of its name: a store's own `action first(n)` or
`action preview(path)` is the store's, called with its arguments, and a
worker's `css.last(kind)` is the worker's.

## Number methods

`toFixed(n)`, `toPrecision(n)`, `toExponential(n)`, `toLocaleString()`,
`toString()`, `valueOf()`.

To convert, use `Number("12")` and `String(n)`, or `"{n}"`. To round, use
`Math.round`, `Math.floor`, `Math.ceil`, `Math.max` and the rest of
`Math`. For text a reader sees, prefer [`format`](#format).

```wf
derived share = (part / whole * 100).toFixed(1)
```

## The built-in types

Eleven types come with the language. Each is a plain JSON value at run
time.

| Type | Written | Methods and fields |
|---|---|---|
| `Date` | `@2026-03-14` | `.year() .month() .day() .weekday()`, `.plus(days: 3)`, `.minus(…)`, `.isBefore(d) .isAfter(d) .isSame(d)`, `.until(d)`, `.startOfDay() .startOfWeek() .startOfMonth() .endOfDay()`, `.native()` |
| `Time` | `@09:30` | `.hour() .minute() .second()`, `.plus(minutes: 30)`, the comparisons |
| `DateTime` | `@2026-03-14T09:30Z` | the above, `.date() .time()`, `.inZone("Europe/Berlin")` |
| `Duration` | `90.minutes`, `3.days`, `250.ms` | `.days() .hours() .minutes() .seconds() .ms()`, `.plus(d)` |
| `Money` | `€12.99`, `$9.99`, `£4.50` | `.plus(m) .minus(m) .times(n) .convert(rate, "USD")`, `.amount`, `.currency` |
| `Url` | a string | `.host() .path() .query()`, `.with(query: { page: 2 })` |
| `Email` | a string | `.domain()` |
| `Color` | `#0F766E` | `.mix(other, 0.2) .lighten(n) .darken(n) .alpha(0.5) .contrast(other)` |
| `Uuid` | `uuid()` | a string's |
| `File` | from `FileUpload` | `.preview()`, `.name`, `.size`, `.type` |
| `Secret` | — | none: it may not be shown, spliced, logged or persisted |

`.plus` and `.minus` take `years`, `months`, `weeks`, `days`, `hours`,
`minutes`, `seconds` and `ms`. A duration is written with `ms`, `seconds`,
`minutes`, `hours`, `days` or `weeks`. What the language computes is a call
(`due.year()`); what the value already carries is a field
(`price.amount`). [Types](/learn/12-types#the-types-the-language-brings-with-it)
has the rest.

```wf
derived checkout = arrival.plus(days: nights)
```

## Browser globals

These names compile to themselves, with no prefix: `window`, `document`,
`console`, `navigator`, `location`, `history`, `screen`, `performance`,
`crypto`, `globalThis`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `JSON`, `Math`,
`Date`, `Intl`, `Symbol`, `Reflect`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`,
`clearTimeout`, `clearInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`,
`cancelAnimationFrame`, `queueMicrotask`, `structuredClone`, `matchMedia`,
`getComputedStyle`, `parseInt`, `parseFloat`, `Array`, `Object`, `String`,
`Number`, `Boolean`, `Promise`, `Error`, `Map`, `Set`, `RegExp`,
`Infinity`, `NaN`, `undefined`, `encodeURIComponent`,
`decodeURIComponent`, `encodeURI`, `decodeURI`, `atob`, `btoa`, `alert`,
`confirm`, `prompt`, `URL`, `URLSearchParams`, `FormData`, `Blob`, `File`,
`FileReader`, `Event`, `CustomEvent`, `AbortController`, `TextEncoder`,
`TextDecoder`, `Notification`.

The checker types each of them as `Any`. A name the program declares
itself wins over a global, and unlike the language's own names, a global
may be the name of a state, a prop or a parameter.

```wf
localStorage.setItem("last-seen", now.date())
```

## Next

[Design tokens](/reference/tokens).

# Runtime API

https://webfluent.monzeromer.dev/reference/runtime

This chapter is the reference for `window.WF`, the runtime every compiled
page calls. Look up a function here when a script of your own, a library's
callback or the browser's console needs to do what a page does — navigate,
show a toast, read a store.

`app.js` opens with the runtime, and the page reaches it as `window.WF`.
This plain script, in `src/`, moves to a route, shows a toast and logs what
a store holds:

```js
// src/support.js
function openHelp() {
  WF.navigate("/about");
  WF.toast("Saved", "success");
  console.log(WF.storeSnapshot("Cart"));
}
```

## Calling the runtime

These rules apply to every function in this chapter:

- **Who calls it.** The compiled pages call the runtime. So may a project
  script under `src/` or in `meta.scripts`, a library's callback, or you in
  the browser's console.
- **Which functions to call.** Most names here are what the compiler emits
  for a language feature, listed so you can read the output. The ones
  meant for your own code are marked **●**.
- **Modules.** The runtime is a set of feature modules. Each table names
  the module a function belongs to, and a build ships only the modules its
  own code reaches. The project's own scripts count: a `WF.toast(…)` in
  `src/support.js` ships `toast`. Only a call the build cannot see — a name
  built from a string, a script loaded from another origin — needs
  `"build": { "runtime": "full" }`
  ([Call WF from a script](/recipes/call-wf-from-a-script)).

## Events the runtime dispatches

`wf:render` is dispatched on `document` once a drawing lands: the first
mount, the takeover of a pre-rendered page, and every route change. Its
`detail` is `{ route, params }`. A script that finds elements itself
listens for it:

```js
// src/highlight-tables.js
document.addEventListener("wf:render", (e) => {
  for (const t of document.querySelectorAll("table.sortable")) t.dataset.route = e.detail.route;
});
```

See also: [JavaScript interop](/recipes/listen-for-wf-render).

## State

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `signal(value)` ● | `core` | A reactive value: call it to read it; `.set(v)`, `.update(f)` and `.subscribe(f)` change and watch it. |
| `computed(fn)` ● | `core` | A value computed from signals, recomputed when they change. |
| `effect(fn)` ● | `core` | Runs `fn`, and again when a signal it read changes. A function `fn` returns is its cleanup, run before the next run and when the effect is disposed. An effect that changes what it reads on every run is stopped after 100 nested runs (with a warning under `wf serve`). |
| `scoped(fn)` | `core` | Runs `fn` in a new scope: what it creates is disposed of with the scope. |
| `onCleanup(fn)` | `core` | Registers `fn` to run when the current scope is disposed. |
| `every(ms, fn)`, `after(ms, fn)` | `core` | A repeating or one-shot timer that stops with the current scope. |
| `listen(target, event, fn, options)` | `core` | An event listener removed with the current scope. |
| `ref()` | `core` | An element handle, filled when the element is made; used as the element itself (`name.focus()`, `name.value`). |

## Elements

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `el(tag, attrs, …children)` | `core` | Makes an element. A function given as an attribute or a child follows the signals it reads. |
| `text(fn)` | `core` | A text node that follows what `fn` reads. |
| `props(given, defaults)` | `core` | A component's props, with defaults filled in. |
| `classes(node, fn)` | `core` | Live classes: the classes `fn` named last time come off, the ones it names now go on. |
| `mark(node, attrs)` | `core` | Puts `data-wf-exit`, `data-wf-delay`, `data-wf-duration` and `data-wf-animate` on a component's root, for the bodies below to play. |
| `rootAttrs(node, attrs)` | `core` | Writes the attributes a component call passes onto the component's root element. |
| `onRoot(node, event, fn)` | `core` | A handler on a component's root element. |
| `bound(control)` | `core` | What a bound control holds, typed: a number field's number (`null` when empty), a select's option value as it was written, otherwise the text. |
| `emit(props, event, …args)` | `core` | Fires a component's declared event. |

## Bodies

What the control-flow statements and slots compile to.

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `when(parent, cond, then, else, anim)` | `when` | `if` / `else`. |
| `held(read)` | `when` | What an `if let` binding reads: the value now, or the last one while the branch leaves. |
| `each(parent, list, item, options)` | `each` | `for`, keyed or not. Keyed items keep their nodes across inserts, removals and moves, and with `live` across a new value too. |
| `show(parent, cond, body, anim)` | `show` | `show`. |
| `match(parent, key, arg, arms)` | `match` | `match`. An arm is called with the value and an accessor of it, and drawn again when the arm changes. |
| `slot(parent, values, render)` | `slot` | A component's slot, drawing the caller's fill. |
| `windowed(node, listFn, itemFn, options)` | `windowed` | A `VirtualList`'s keyed `for`. |

## Keys, focus and gestures

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `onKey(node, combination, fn)` | `keys` | `on key("mod+k")`. |
| `keyIs(event, combination)` | `keys` | `keyIs(e, "mod+k")`: whether a key event is that combination. |
| `keyLabel(combination)` | `keys` | `keyLabel("mod+k")`: how this system writes the combination (`⌘K`, `Ctrl+K`). |
| `keyAria(combination)` | `keys` | The combination as `aria-keyshortcuts` writes it, for a drawn `shortcut:`. |
| `trapFocus(node, read)` | `layer` | `trapFocus: open`. |
| `gesture(node, name, fn)` | `gesture` | `on longpress(p)`, `on swipe(s)`, `on receive(d)`, `on dragmove(d)`. |
| `draggable(node, value, options)`, `dropTarget(node, options)` | `gesture` | `drag:`, `dragGroup:`, `dropValue:`, `dropAxis:`, `dropInside:`. |
| `splitter(node, read, write, options)` | `gesture` | `Splitter(bind:, min:, max:, reset:)`. |

## Motion

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `animate(target, name, duration)` ● | `motion` | Plays an animation now, and returns a handle with `play()`, `cancel()` and `finished`. |
| `replay(node, name, duration)` ● | `motion` | Plays an element's animation again from the start (`replayAnimation` in `.wf`). |
| `animateIn(node, name, duration, delay, easing)`, `animateOut(…)` | `motion` | Enter and exit animations. |
| `expand(node, open, duration, easing)` | `motion` | Opens or closes a box to its measured height. |
| `countTo(node, from, to, duration, format)`, `counted(node, valueFn, duration, format)` | `motion` | A number that counts to its new value. |
| `onEnterView(node, name, duration, delay, easing)` | `motion` | Plays an animation when the element is scrolled into view. |
| `shared(node, name)` | `motion` | An element carried across a route change. |

## Routing and pages

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `navigate(path)` ● | `core` | Moves to a route (a page load in a static build). |
| `params()` ● | `router` | The current route's parameters. |
| `router(routes, container, options)` | `router` | The router `Router` compiles to; `options.transition` is `fade` or `slide`. |
| `activeLink(a, href, prefix)` | `router` | Keeps a link's `.active` class and `aria-current`. |
| `playRoute(options, page)` | `router` | Internal: plays a `Router(transition:)`, which the compiled router passes as `play:`. |
| `page(name, fn)`, `loadPage(name, cb)`, `loadSheet(name, cb)` | `pages` | Page chunks and their stylesheets. |
| `setBasePath(path)`, `setSsgMode(on)` | `core` | Set at boot from the config. |

## Browser values

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `viewport()`, `query()`, `hash()`, `network()` | `browser` | What the language's `viewport`, `query`, `hash` and `network` hold. |
| `now(options)` | `browser` | `now`, kept current every minute, or as often as `options.every` asks. |
| `theme()` | `theme` | The theme the reader chose. |
| `setTheme(choice)` ● | `theme` | Switches the theme: `"dark"`, `"light"` or `"system"`, kept across visits. |

## Data and connections

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `resource(url, options)` | `net` | A resource: `{ state, data, error, refreshing, pending, items, hasMore, reload, loadMore, invalidate, cancel }`. |
| `request(url, options)`, `fetch(url, options)` ● | `net` | A request through the engine — retries, timeouts, cache, typed errors — that resolves to the parsed body. `await fetch(…)` in an action compiles to `request`. |
| `optimistic(holder, change)` | `net` | Shows a change at once, rolled back if the action throws. |
| `attempt(fn)` | `net` | Runs an action so that a throw rolls back its optimistic changes. |
| `send(url, options)` | `http` | The engine's request itself. |
| `invalidate(prefix)` | `http` | Drops cached answers: every one with no argument, or each key equal to or starting with `prefix`. |
| `beacon(url, data)` ● | `http` | A post that survives the page unloading. |
| `api(definition)` | `api` | The service an `api` declaration compiles to. |
| `ws(url, options)`, `sse(url, options)`, `broadcast(name, options)` | `api` | A socket, a stream of events, a channel between tabs. |
| `rtc(options)` | `peer` | A peer: a WebRTC data channel. |
| `worker(url, options)` | `worker` | A `worker`: a script of the site run beside the page. |

## Stores

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `store(name, define, options)` | `store` | A store, built the first time something reads it. |
| `dropRouteStores()` | `store` | Drops the `scope: .route` stores, on a route change. |
| `watchStores(fn)` ● | `store` | Calls `fn` with every action and the state on each side of it, and returns the function that stops it. Nothing is recorded while nothing is watching. |
| `storeSnapshot(name?)` ● | `store` | What every store, or one, holds. |
| `restoreStore(name, values)` ● | `store` | Puts a store back to what it held. |
| `persist(base, initial, policy)` | `keep` | A `persist` value's storage, versions and migrations. |

## Widgets and layers

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `toast(message, tone, ms)` ● | `toast` | Shows a toast in tone `"success"`, `"danger"`, `"warning"` or `"info"` (the default), for `ms` milliseconds (3000 by default). |
| `announce(text)` ● | `announce` | Says `text` to screen readers, politely. |
| `dialog(el, read, write)`, `tabs(nav, active)` | `overlay` | What `Modal` and `Dialog`, and `Tabs`, compile to. |
| `popup(root, trigger, open)` | `overlay` | Closes a popup on Escape or a click outside, and returns focus to its trigger. |
| `layer(el, read, write, options)` | `layer` | A layer drawn in the browser's top layer at an anchor or a point: what `Popover` compiles to. |
| `menu`, `submenu`, `tooltip` | `layer` | What `Menu`, `Menu.Sub` and `Tooltip` compile to. |
| `placeAt(anchor, size, viewport, placement, offset)` | `layer` | Where a layer of `size` goes against `anchor`, flipped and slid to stay on screen. |
| `uid(prefix)` | `layer` | An id no other element of the page has. |
| `drawer(panel, toggle, scrim)` | `drawer` | Wires an off-canvas panel to its toggle button: a `Sidebar`'s or a `Navbar`'s links on a narrow screen. |
| `carousel(root, options)` | `carousel` | What `Carousel` compiles to. |
| `field(control, options)`, `choiceError(label, check)` | `field` | A control's label, hint and error; a `Checkbox` or `Switch`'s rule message. |
| `form(options)`, `validate(read, rules, options)` | `form` | A `Form` handle and a `validate` block's rules. |
| `askRules(read, rules, fault, remote, pending)` | `form` | Internal: asks a `validate` block's `async` rules, which the compiled form passes as `ask:`. |

## Safety

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `safeUrl(url)` ● | `core` | The URL where a browser may follow it, `""` where it may not. |
| `safePicture(url)` | `core` | As `safeUrl`, and also a picture carried in its address (`data:image/…`), for an image's `src`. |
| `allowSchemes(schemes)` | `core` | Adds an app's own schemes (from `meta.frame`) to those `safeUrl` allows; called once at boot. |
| `sanitize(html)` ● | `sanitize` | Markup through the allow-list. |
| `jsonAttr(raw)` | `core` | An attribute holding JSON, as the prop it stands for. |

`safeUrl` and `sanitize` each have a build-time twin, and both twins are
held to one shared table of cases.

## Text and formatting

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `markdown(text)` ● | `text` | Renders the language's Markdown to HTML. |
| `highlight(code, lang)` ● | `text` | Colours `wf`, `json`, `bash` or `css` with `wf-tok-*` spans. |
| `format(value, style, option)` ● | `format` | Formats a value in the page's locale, as `format` in `.wf`. |
| `ago(date)` ● | `format` | A relative time in the page's locale: `3 minutes ago`. |
| `locales(default, tables)` | `i18n` | Sets up `WF.i18n`, with `t`, `locale`, `dir` and `setLocale`. |

## Values

Each of these is a function of the value it works on.

| Functions | Module | What they are |
|---|---|---|
| `sortBy`, `groupBy`, `unique`, `take`, `first`, `last`, `capitalize`, `truncate`, `dedent`, `lines`, `words`, `range`, `removeAt` | `helpers` | The list and string helpers, and `a..b` ranges. |
| `setIn(target, path, value)`, `mutated(list, method, args)` | `helpers` | A state changed in place — `form.name = v`, `items.sort()` — as a copy with that place changed. |
| `year`, `month`, `day`, `weekday`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `plus`, `minus`, `isBefore`, `isAfter`, `isSame`, `until`, `startOfDay`, `startOfWeek`, `startOfMonth`, `endOfDay`, `inZone`, `native` | `scalars` | The methods of `Date`, `Time` and `DateTime`. |
| `days`, `hours`, `minutes`, `seconds`, `ms` | `scalars` | The methods of `Duration`. |
| `money`, `times`, `convert` | `scalars` | `Money`. |
| `host`, `path`, `domain`, `urlWith`, `urlQuery` | `scalars` | `Url` and `Email`; `.with()` and `.query()`. |
| `mix`, `lighten`, `darken`, `alpha`, `contrast` | `scalars` | `Color`. |
| `preview`, `uuid`, `dateOf`, `timeOf` | `scalars` | A `File`'s preview, `uuid()`, `.date()` and `.time()`. |
| `caseOf(v)`, `payload(v)` | `core` | An enum value's case and its payload. |

## Boot and interop

| Function | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `mount(fn, container)` | `core` | Draws the app into `container`. |
| `mainOf(root)` | `core` | The `<main>` the pages draw into: `root` itself, the `<main>` inside it, or a new one. |
| `live(node)` | `core` | Marks `node` as held by something, so a takeover keeps the drawn node rather than the painted one. |
| `hydrate(fn, container)`, `hydrating(root)` | `hydrate` | Draws beside a pre-rendered page and takes it over in place. |
| `attach(node, mount, update, cleanup)` | `host` | What `mount:`, `update:` and `cleanup:` compile to, on `Host` or any element; a component's fragment is attached at its root element. |
| `portal(box, read)` | `host` | What `Portal` compiles to (below). |
| `head(tags)` | `head` | A page's own `head { }` tags. |
| `picture(asset, options)` | `picture` | An `image`'s `<picture>`. |
| `offline(options)`, `update()`, `clearQueued()` | `offline` | The service worker, the update flow, and forgetting the writes kept offline. |
| `loadAfter(scripts)` | `later` | Loads the `meta.scripts` entries marked `"load": "after"` once the page has painted. |
| `__debug`, `__reg` | `debug` | For WebFluent Studio. |

`portal(box, read)` keeps `box` in the element, or `ref:` handle, that
`read()` names. It reads `read()` again when what it reads changes and once
the drawing is over, keeps the box aside while `read()` is `null`, and takes
it away with its scope. It returns what runs the lifetimes its block asked
for while it was drawn.

The `icons` module has no functions: it is the table of glyphs, holding
only the icons the program names.

## Next

[Grammar](/reference/grammar) — every statement and expression of the language.
